minutes.headline: Board of Health approved all septic variances, the FY budget, and letting the assistant sign rubbish permits during COVID.
minutes.summary: The Board of Health met remotely and heard several Title 5 septic variance requests, each approved by roll call. It discussed whether old wells may be kept as deed-restricted irrigation wells. It also approved the minutes, the budget submission and rubbish license signing, and heard a COVID update from the agent.

votes.motion: Approve variance request for 33 Baltwell Street (groundwater and wetlands offset)
Grant the four variances requested for 31 Hickory Hills lot
Accept variances for 17 West Street Terrace
Authorize the administrative assistant to sign rubbish permits for the duration of the COVID crisis
Grant request to keep the well at 166 South Railroad as a deed-restricted agricultural/irrigation well
Grant the two Title 5 variances for 299 Page Street
Allow the two wells at 299 Page Street to continue as irrigation-only wells with deed restriction

budget_items.what_was_said: The submitted budget increases the administrative assistant's hours by six per week, a repeated request that was cut in past years.
The assistant shifted money among the board's small fixed lines, moving more into emergency preparedness and away from rabid animal control and office supplies.
An anticipated increase was put in for Nashoba, to be confirmed at the end of January.
CARES money no longer has to be returned until next year, so the effect on town hours is unknown.
Discontinuing an artesian well would cost the homeowner a sum the speaker put at roughly a thousand dollars.

decisions.decision: Designer will talk to his clients about keeping or destroying the well; the board will consider an irrigation-well policy later, not tonight.
Members agreed informally that applicant hearings could be scheduled at about ten-minute intervals.
Whether to revisit commercial recycling regulations is left for the first March meeting.
Applicants are asked to cite the specific Title 5 regulation being varied in their letters.
Businesses violating mask rules should appear before the board before any fine or permit action.

what_happened.line: The Board of Health approved every Title 5 septic variance before it, including 33 Baltwell Street, 31 Hickory Hills, 17 West Street Terrace and 299 Page Street.
The board voted to keep the wells at 166 South Railroad and 299 Page Street as irrigation-only wells with deed restrictions.
The board approved the budget as submitted, which includes more hours for the administrative assistant and an anticipated increase for Nashoba.
The board authorized the administrative assistant to sign rubbish permits for the duration of the COVID crisis.
Members said businesses that break mask rules should appear before the board before any fine or permit action.

why_it_matters: The irrigation-well votes were made case by case, with no written policy yet, so the rules for keeping old wells on a property remain unsettled for future applicants.

The approved budget asks for more administrative assistant hours, a request that was cut in past years, so it affects what the town budget, mostly taxes, pays for public health staffing and whether it passes at Town Meeting.
watch_next: Whether to revisit commercial recycling regulations is left for the first March meeting.
The Nashoba assessment increase in the budget is to be confirmed at the end of January.
